messages:
maria-peopleops: Hey folks — quick Q. New hire (international) just submitted a marriage certificate issued in Spanish. They ask whether a scanned translated copy is OK for benefits enrollment, or do we need an apostille/certified translation? Also wondering if this affects spouse vs domestic partner classification for benefits/tax.
claire-benefits: Short answer: we usually need a certified English translation + either an apostille or embassy notarization for foreign marriage docs, depending on country. Which country is it? :thinking_face:
maria-peopleops: Chile — they submitted a scanned pdf from the civil registry, no apostille.
claire-benefits: Chilean docs typically require an apostille for US acceptance. We also need the translator's certification if translation not done by an official translator. Upload into the benefits portal under "Dependent Docs". If they can't get apostille in time, we can provisionally enroll for 30 days pending verification in some cases — need payroll/HR signoff.
alex-payroll: FYI payroll: provisional enrollment affects pre-tax deductions. We need signed attestation from the employee that the spouse will provide apostille within 30 days, and we log it as pending in Workday so payroll can code it correctly. Without SSN/ITIN we can't add them to payroll records but benefits enrollment can proceed if Claire signs off.
roger-hr: To confirm: 30-day provisional is allowed for QLEs when documentation is delayed. Maria, if you want to do that, add a note in the case and tag @alex-payroll & @claire-benefits. We will escalate if >30 days.
maria-peopleops: Got it. I'll ask the employee to obtain an apostille. If they can't, is embassy notarization acceptable as a fallback?
claire-benefits: Embassy notarization is acceptable for many countries, yes — but apostille is preferred. If embassy notarization is used, we need to see chain-of-custody info. Also accept US-issued marriage certificates if they were married in the US consulate.
alex-payroll: Also remind the new hire to request an SSN/ITIN asap. For tax classification: if the marriage is legally recognized by the US (apostille/translation + valid civil certificate), they are spouse for benefits and tax withholding looks at marital status for payroll taxes — they should consult a tax advisor for personal liability. Payroll needs the supporting docs before moving from provisional to permanent payroll status.
claire-benefits: Upload steps for reference:
```
1) Employee goes to Benefits Portal > Documents > Add Dependent
2) Upload original marriage certificate (scanned) + certified English translation
3) Upload apostille or embassy notarization
4) Add SSN/ITIN when available
5) In the notes field, mark "Provisionally enrolled - docs pending"
```
maria-peopleops: Perfect — I'll send these steps to the hire and request proof of embassy/notary or apostille. Tagging you both when they reply. :white_check_mark:
hr-bot: Reminder: submit enrollment changes within 30 days of QLE to ensure retro coverage. See policy: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/qle
roger-hr: Thanks team. If the employee hits snags getting an apostille, ping me and we'll help with next steps (expedited processing options).
